parsed.notes: readability: Naming and assertion messages are clear and mostly accurate (e.g. pair_finder.py `_is_real_numeric_scalar`, `_validate_catalog`), but several messages are misleading — the same-length assertion always reports the x/y lengths regardless of which fields actually mismatch (`f"arrays must have same length, got {lengths[0]}, {lengths[1]} for x, y"`), and the docstrings are one-liners that don't convey the extensive validation rules actually implemented, requiring the bloated root-level .md files to explain intent that should live in code comments/docstrings. maintainability: `_is_real_numeric_scalar` is reused across both validators (good), but `_validate_catalog`/`_validate_config` are long monolithic functions with repeated per-field boilerplate (each of max_sep/mass_ratio_min/log_mass_min/log_mass_max/mass_bin_width repeats identical scalar+finite+range assert triplets instead of a shared parametrized helper), and three committed root-level markdown/shell artifacts (IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md, VERIFICATION.md, commit.sh) are process cruft/dead weight not part of the actual library.
